cards.text: It's the eighth day, friend. Aaron and his sons just spent seven days at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting being ordained as priests. Now Moses, Israel's leader, calls in Aaron the priest, Aaron's sons and the elders of Israel.
Moses tells Aaron to take a young bull and a ram for himself and present them before the LORD. My first day in this bakery, my opening act was setting off the smoke alarm. TWICE.

cards.question: Moses gives one rule for both of Aaron's animals, the young bull and the ram. What does each one have to be?
Moses tells Aaron the young bull is for a ___ offering and the ram is for a ___ offering.

cards.text: Then Aaron tells the Israelites what they need to bring: a male goat for a sin offering, a calf and a lamb for a burnt offering, an ox and a ram for a peace offering, and a grain offering mixed with oil. Friend, that's not a delivery, that's a whole PARADE.

cards.question: Moses tells the Israelites why they need to bring all those offerings today. What reason does he give?

answers.text: Today the LORD will appear to them
Today the camp will set out

cards.text: So they bring everything Moses commanded to the front of the Tent of Meeting. Goats, calves, an ox. I bet you could hear that walk from the next tribe over.

cards.question: At the Tent of Meeting, only Aaron and the elders come near and stand before the LORD.

cards.text: Moses says, “This is what the LORD has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD may appear to you.” Then he tells Aaron to approach the altar and sacrifice his sin offering and his burnt offering.

cards.question: Moses says Aaron's own sin offering and burnt offering make atonement for Aaron and for the people.

cards.text: So Aaron approaches the altar and slaughters the calf as a sin offering for himself. The whole congregation is watching, so no pressure, Aaron. NO pressure.

cards.question: Aaron's sons bring him the blood of the calf. Where does Aaron put it with his finger?

answers.text: On the horns of the altar

cards.text: He pours out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar. Then he burns the fat, the kidneys and the lobe of the liver on the altar, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

cards.question: The calf's fat goes on the altar. Where does Aaron burn up the calf's flesh and hide?

answers.text: At the base of the altar

cards.text: Next comes the burnt offering. His sons bring the blood, Aaron splatters it on all sides of the altar, and they bring him the offering piece by piece, head included, and he burns it all on the altar.

cards.question: Aaron washes the burnt offering's entrails and legs before he burns them on the altar.

cards.text: Aaron's own offerings are done. Now he presents the people's offering, starting with the male goat for the people's sin offering.

cards.question: Aaron slaughters the people's goat and offers it for sin the same way as his own sin offering.

cards.text: He offers the people's burnt offering according to the ordinance, then presents the grain offering. A crowd that big, and Aaron STILL sticks to the recipe. I respect a man who sticks to the recipe.

cards.question: How much of the people's grain offering does Aaron burn on the altar?

cards.text: Then Aaron slaughters the ox and the ram as the people's peace offering and splatters the blood on all sides of the altar. His sons place the fat portions on the breasts, and Aaron burns the fat on the altar.

cards.question: With the fat burned, what does Aaron do with the breasts and the right thigh of the peace offering?

cards.text: Sin offering, burnt offering, peace offering, all done. Friend, if I finished a list that long, you'd find me asleep in the flour bin.

cards.question: With every offering made, Aaron faces the people. What does he do?

answers.text: Lifts up his hands and blesses them
Sends them back to their tents

cards.text: Then Aaron steps down. He and Moses go into the Tent of Meeting.

cards.question: When Moses and Aaron come out of the Tent of Meeting, they bless the people.

cards.text: And then it happens, friend. The glory of the LORD appears to all the people, just like Moses said it would.

cards.question: Fire comes out from the presence of the LORD. What does it consume on the altar?

answers.text: The burnt offering and the fat portions
The breasts and the right thigh

cards.question: All the people see the fire from the LORD. What do they do?

answers.text: Shout for joy and fall facedown

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause for now, friend. The priests have only just started their service, and trust me, this story isn't finished.

findings.problem: The card says Aaron and his sons spent seven days at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting being ordained. That fact comes from Leviticus 8:33-35, outside the passage, but the card cites only Leviticus 9:1. The outside fact has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card says Aaron tells the Israelites what to bring. In Leviticus 9:3 Moses tells Aaron to speak to the Israelites. The text never says Aaron did it, so the card should present this as Moses's instruction, not as something Aaron does.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question says Moses tells the Israelites why they need to bring the offerings. In Leviticus 9:3-4, Moses gives Aaron these words to say to the Israelites. The text shows Moses speaking to Aaron, not to the Israelites, so the card contradicts it. It also clashes with card 5, which says Aaron tells them.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: "Goats, calves, an ox" uses plurals as fact. The text lists one male goat and one calf for the people (Leviticus 9:3). The plurals stretch the text outside the joke line.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: One story card carries four moments: the sons bring the blood, Aaron splatters it, they bring the pieces, and he burns them. That is more than two things happening.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: One story card carries four moments: Aaron slaughters the ox and ram, splatters the blood, the fat portions are placed on the breasts, and Aaron burns the fat. That is more than two things happening.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: Stop 2 has 5 multiple choice cards, 2 true or false cards and no fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells nothing from the passage, but it cites Leviticus 9:24. The citation rule says a story card cites the verses it tells, and this card tells none.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line, what should its verses field cite: the last verse of the passage, or something else?
